title: With LUKS-encrypted disk's password saved in KWallet, mounting the disk shows a password dialog with the password already pre-populated in the password field, instead of just decrypting it without asking for interaction
line: Encrypted drives whose password is saved in the wallet now unlock right away, without a password dialog to confirm.
explanation: The soliduiserver kded module only used the wallet password to prefill the passphrase dialog, so the user still had to press OK. Sending the password straight back is not trivial: Solid waits synchronously for showPassphraseDialog to return before it accepts a passphraseReply, so replying from inside that call (as the old draft !2745 did) deadlocks or is ignored. The module now sends the saved password with a queued, non-blocking passphraseReply right after the call returns, and watches the device's setupDone; if that unlock fails, the next attempt shows the dialog again, prefilled, so a changed passphrase can be corrected and re-saved.

commits.message:
soliduiserver: unlock with the saved password without asking

A LUKS passphrase saved in the wallet was only prefilled in the dialog,
so it still had to be confirmed. It is now sent right after Solid's call
returns, and the dialog only comes back once that password has failed.

BUG: 467098

media.caption: Mount and Open on a stick whose passphrase is in the wallet: the dialog still appears, prefilled, waiting for OK
Same click with the fix: the stick unlocks and mounts and Dolphin opens it, with no dialog

review.text: This is a strong approach that solves the synchronous Solid D-Bus deadlock that stalled draft !2745 by queuing a non-blocking passphraseReply right after showPassphraseDialog returns and watching Solid::StorageAccess::setupDone for failures. However, clearing m_failedSavedPasswords unconditionally before the fallback dialog finishes means canceling the dialog or unlocking once without saving causes the next mount to silently fail with the stale wallet password again. In addition, capturing Solid::Device by value inside a self-disconnecting lambda on access creates a reference cycle that leaks until kded6 exits if setupDone never fires.
changes: Do not remove udi from m_failedSavedPasswords before the fallback dialog succeeds or updates the wallet; track the failed saved password per udi (or clear the failure entry only when a new password is saved or unlock succeeds) so Cancel or unlocking without 'Remember password' still shows the dialog on the next attempt.

Use Qt::SingleShotConnection instead of std::make_shared<QMetaObject::Connection>() and clean up any pending setupDone connection on Solid::DeviceNotifier::deviceRemoved (and when replacing an existing pending attempt for the same udi) so the captured Solid::Device cannot leak if setupDone never arrives.

reviews.text: Right repo and a sound mechanism: Solid only accepts passphraseReply after the blocking showPassphraseDialog call has returned, so a queued reply after the call returns, plus watching setupDone for failures, works and matches what the reporter and the duplicates ask for. But auto-unlock makes the wallet entry stronger than before, and onPassphraseDialogCompleted still never removes it: if the user corrects a wrong saved password with 'Remember password' unchecked, the stale wrong one stays in the wallet and every mount after that goes fail, dialog, fail, dialog. Also, a wrong saved password costs the user a 'Could not mount' error and a second click before the dialog appears, which maintainers will likely question.
changes: In onPassphraseDialogCompleted, remove the SolidLuks/<uuid> wallet entry when keep is false and an entry exists, so unchecking 'Remember password' stops the automatic unlock
Spell out the wrong-password flow (one error, then the dialog on the next attempt) in the commit message or MR, or find a way to show the dialog right away
Make sure the setupDone connection is dropped if no setupDone arrives (e.g. reuse or replace a per-udi connection), so repeated attempts don't pile up connections
